summary.tldr: Sets trial time limits in the Criminal Code and requires courts to stop cases that run too long, with some exceptions.
what_it_does: Sets a 30 month ceiling for trials in superior court and an 18 month ceiling for trials in provincial court, measured from when a charge is laid to the expected or actual end of trial.
Requires judges to stay proceedings if those limits are exceeded, unless the prosecutor shows exceptional circumstances that make the delay reasonable.
Excludes delay caused solely by the defence, or delay the defence waives, from the time limit calculation.
Exempts primary designated offences, as defined in the Criminal Code, from the new time limit rules.
Declares that the exemption for primary designated offences applies despite the Charter right to be tried within a reasonable time.
summary.background: The bill says it codifies the Supreme Court of Canada’s framework in R. v. Jordan on the right of an accused to be tried within a reasonable time. It adds a new Part XVI.1 to the Criminal Code.
